featured_videos.title: These Raw Meat Diets Look Insane (But They Actually Work)
featured_videos.creator: FaceIQ
featured_videos.editorial_title: These Raw Meat Diets Look Insane (But They Actually Work)
featured_videos.commentary: Okay, so the comments are absolutely roasting this one, and honestly? They're not wrong. There's this weird energy where people are conflating "raw meat works" with "you need to do EVERYTHING extreme to get results," and it's kind of missing the point. The real conversation should be about what actually moves the needle, not whether you're raw or cooked or doing whatever bizarre optimization du jour. Some of the comments about lifestyle stuff beyond diet (cotton clothing, cookware, plastics) are actually hitting on something important though, that diet alone doesn't fix everything if everything else in your environment is working against you. The carnivore community gets this right most of the time, we focus on the meat but we know electrolytes matter, sleep matters, stress matters, all of it. Raw meat diets definitely work for some people, but let's not pretend the magic is in the rawness instead of just finally eating real food.

featured_videos.title: If Humans Aren't Carnivores, Explain This!
featured_videos.creator: Bart Kay - Health Science
featured_videos.editorial_title: If Humans Aren't Carnivores, Explain This!
featured_videos.commentary: The community's right here, and it matters. People are asking for clarity, not a three-hour rabbit hole. Bart's doing exactly what the movement needs: short, structured, shareable content that actually answers the question "why carnivore?" instead of burying it under layers of nuance. When someone's skeptical friend asks "but aren't we supposed to eat plants?", having a five-minute video that covers the actual evidence beats trying to explain trophic levels over dinner. The format works because it respects people's time while not dumbing down the science. That's the entry point we've been missing.

featured_videos.title: These 10 Foods Make Up 90% of My Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.creator: Jenny Mitich
featured_videos.editorial_title: These 10 Foods Make Up 90% of My Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.commentary: Real talk: the best part of this video isn't what Jenny eats, it's what the community caught onto. That joke about "leftover steak" landed because everyone knows the truth, right? You don't actually have leftovers on carnivore. But here's what's actually resonating in the comments: people are celebrating how boring it is in the best way possible. One person nailed it saying simplicity is the most underrated advantage, and honestly, that's the whole thing. You're not spending mental energy deciding what to eat, not washing a dozen pans, not fighting cravings at the grocery store. It's ground beef, eggs, bacon, repeat. The "restriction" argument carnivore critics love to make completely falls apart when you realize most of us eat the same 10-15 foods anyway, and we're actually happy about it.

featured_videos.title: JUNE 2026 NEW Costco Items For Low Carb Weight Loss
featured_videos.creator: Low Carb Love
featured_videos.editorial_title: JUNE 2026 NEW Costco Items For Low Carb Weight Loss
featured_videos.commentary: One thing I'm noticing in the comments is the real tension between convenience and ingredient quality, and honestly, that's where most people get stuck. The 55lb weight loss is incredible, but that commenter asking about clean ingredients has a point, because ultra-processed Costco meals can stall progress for some people even on low carb. Here's what I've seen work: use those quick items as scaffolding while you're building the habit, then gradually shift toward whole foods as you get comfortable. Costco's rotisserie chickens, eggs, and ground beef are legitimately solid foundations, and they're cheap enough that you don't have to choose between budget and results.

featured_videos.title: What's Wrong With Keto?! (This May Upset Some People)
featured_videos.creator: Chris Cooking Nashville
featured_videos.editorial_title: What's Wrong With Keto?! (This May Upset Some People)
featured_videos.commentary: Chris nailed something the community clearly needed to hear. The comments section is full of people saying "thank you for giving us permission to not be perfect," and that's the real win here. Keto got 75 pounds off someone. Their friend lost weight eating junk with IF. Another viewer reversed stage 4 kidney disease on keto, then switched to carnivore with fermented foods. None of those wins are invalidated because someone mixed protocols or bent the rules. The gatekeeping around diet labels has gotten ridiculous, and what matters is that people are ditching processed food and taking their metabolic health seriously. Whether you're strict carnivore, mostly keto with some wiggle room, or doing a mix that works for your body, you're still winning compared to the standard American diet. That's the conversation we should be having.

featured_videos.title: I Did Not Expect This...
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.commentary: The weight loss numbers are solid, but the real story in these comments isn't about the scale. People are tearing up because they're watching family healing happen in real time, and that's what carnivore actually does for people when it works. Larry reconnecting with his brother Eric, the community cheering them on, someone mentioning they healed migraines and lost 120 pounds, someone else going strict in June and already down 6.6 pounds. This isn't performative. When you remove the food noise, you get clarity, energy, and sometimes the space to repair relationships that matter. That's the stuff you don't see in weight loss before-and-afters.
